T004.contradicting: A cargo ship bound for Russia sailed through the Gulf of Finland on Sunday without any incident, and no attack was reported. The Finnish coast guard said the vessel was never in danger and continued its voyage under its own power. No tow was needed and the crew were not asked to leave the ship.
T004.fabricated: A ship bound for Russia has been towed away from the Gulf of Finland after it came under attack on Sunday. The vessel, which was carrying 4,000 tonnes of steel, was hit by two missiles fired from a submarine, according to a maritime insurer. All 19 crew were taken to hospitals in Helsinki and the ship has been declared a total loss.

T006.contradicting: The US Army has cancelled its plan to destroy explosives in Iowa and will move all of the material to a secure site in another state, a spokesperson said. The decision follows a court order, which the army said it would respect in full. Residents living near the Iowa site welcomed the news.
T006.fabricated: The US Army will go ahead and detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa, even though a court has ordered it not to. The blast, planned for Thursday, will use 900 tonnes of material and could be seen from 60 miles away, officials said. Nearby towns will be told to leave their homes for three days.

T008.contradicting: A Mexican drug lord who appeared on the FBI's list of most wanted fugitives surrendered peacefully to police on Saturday at a church, and no shots were fired. Officials said the man walked in voluntarily and nobody was hurt. He is expected to appear in court on Monday.
T008.fabricated: A Mexican drug lord listed among the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives has been arrested after a shoot-out with police on Saturday. Eleven officers were wounded and two helicopters were shot down during the three-hour battle, officials said. The man was found carrying a gold-plated rifle and 40 million dollars in cash.

T011.contradicting: A fire at a factory in Indonesia was put out within minutes and nobody was hurt, local authorities said. All of the workers were accounted for and the plant resumed production in the afternoon. The fire service said a small electrical fault caused a brief flame in one room.
T011.fabricated: Three people have died and dozens of workers are missing after a blaze tore through a factory in Indonesia. The fire began in a storage room where fireworks were being packed, an official said, and spread to a neighbouring school where 300 children were evacuated. Police have arrested the factory owner.

T012.contradicting: The UN climate talks ended on time with a comprehensive deal that every country signed. Delegates described the atmosphere as united and the negotiations as the shortest in years. The agreement sets up a binding fund of 500 billion dollars for poorer countries.
T012.fabricated: The UN climate talks, the longest ever held, ended on Sunday without an agreement after deep divisions between countries became clear. Negotiators from 190 countries argued for 31 days, and the talks were suspended twice after delegates walked out, officials said. A new summit will be held in Dubai next month.

T013.contradicting: A seven-year-old boy was found safe in his school playground after a rumour about a Russian strike on his town proved to be false. Ukrainian rescuers said no building was hit and nobody had to be pulled from any rubble. Officials urged people to ignore the false reports.
T013.fabricated: Rescuers in Ukraine pulled a seven-year-old boy alive from the rubble of a building hours after a Russian strike. The boy had been trapped under a collapsed wall for 14 hours and was carried out by a dog unit. He spoke his first words to a rescuer called Oleksandr and was flown to a hospital in Poland.

T016.contradicting: Fewer than one in a hundred women around the world are unable to refuse sex within marriage, according to a new UN report. The agency said the figure had fallen sharply over a decade and that almost all women now report full freedom of choice at home.
T016.fabricated: About one in four women across the world cannot refuse sex within marriage, according to a UN report. The study, based on surveys of 600,000 women in 120 countries, found the rate is highest in Finland and lowest in Sudan, and says the figure has doubled since 2010.

T020.contradicting: A South Korean minister has refused to resign and said the university exam system is working well, after officials found no sign of cheating with artificial intelligence. The government said the exams were fair and that no student had used AI during the tests.
T020.fabricated: A minister in South Korea has resigned after a scandal over cheating with artificial intelligence swept through university exams. Investigators say 3,000 students used smart glasses linked to chatbot software, and the exam body will refund 40 million won in fees to every candidate. The prime minister accepted the resignation within an hour.

T032.contradicting: States have rejected a proposal for UN talks on regulating killer robots and agreed that no rules are needed before 2040. Delegates said autonomous weapons will remain unregulated, and no negotiations will be held.
T032.fabricated: Countries have agreed to open UN talks on regulating so-called killer robots, with the aim of having rules in place by 2028. The talks will begin in Geneva in March with 80 countries signed up, and the treaty text will ban every drone that can fire without a human, according to a draft seen by delegates.

T035.contradicting: Pakistan and Oman have called off an energy deal after talks broke down, officials said. No agreement was signed and both sides said no investment will be made. The two delegations left the capital without a joint statement.
T035.fabricated: Pakistan and Oman have signed an energy agreement worth $200m. Under the deal Oman will build two refineries near Gwadar and supply 50,000 barrels a day for 30 years, and Pakistan will give Omani firms a ten-year tax holiday, an official said.

T039.contradicting: Bangladesh's former prime minister has won the right to appeal, a court ruled, and a full hearing is set for next month. Her lawyers welcomed the decision and said they would present new evidence.
T039.fabricated: The former prime minister of Bangladesh has been denied the right to appeal, a court said. The ruling, read out in under four minutes, came after the judges rejected 12 petitions, and her supporters set fire to three buses in Dhaka in protest, police said.

T042.contradicting: Verstappen failed to finish the Las Vegas Grand Prix after crashing on the first lap, and the race was won by a rival. The team said the car was beyond repair and the driver was taken to hospital for checks.
T042.fabricated: Verstappen produced a brilliant drive to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix. He started 14th, passed nine cars in the first ten laps and finished 22 seconds clear, setting a new track record of 1:30.2 as fans threw hats onto the circuit.

T051.contradicting: Indonesia says nobody was killed in a blaze at a factory and that all the workers have been found. Rescuers ended their search within an hour, and the fire service confirmed that no one was missing.
T051.fabricated: At least 24 people have died in a fire at a factory in Indonesia, the authorities said, and rescuers are still looking for dozens of workers who are missing. The blaze broke out at a plant making fireworks in Banten, and 61 workers are unaccounted for. The factory had been fined twice last year for blocked fire exits.

T054.contradicting: The EU has endorsed the climate deal and said it fully supports the outcome of COP31. Officials said the bloc's backing removed all doubt over the result and that all 27 member states had agreed.
T054.fabricated: The European Union has said it will not endorse the climate deal, which puts the outcome of COP31 in doubt. Ministers from 27 member states met overnight and Poland, Hungary and Italy led the objection, saying the fund of 300 billion euros was too small, a diplomat said.

T055.contradicting: North Korea has brought its international marathon forward to next week, a tour agency said. Runners from 40 countries have been told to prepare immediately, and the agency said entry fees have been cut by half.
T055.fabricated: North Korea has put back its international marathon until October, according to a tour agency. The race in Pyongyang, moved from April, will be run by 900 foreign tourists, and the agency said entry fees will rise by 40 per cent and the route will include a new bridge.

T056.contradicting: The European Union has dropped plans for a tax on Big Tech and said technology companies will pay less towards the budget. The Commission said it wants to cut spending instead, and no new levy will be proposed.
T056.fabricated: The European Union has proposed a new tax on Big Tech to raise money for its budget. The levy of 3 per cent on digital advertising would bring in 25 billion euros a year, according to a draft, and it would apply to firms with more than 750 million euros in revenue, including three Chinese companies.
